title: KV page placement and payload
description: Distinguish logical positions, physical storage and the live or unused parts of a reserved KV pool.

terms.definition: A key/value cache that divides logical token positions into fixed-size pages and looks up each page's physical placement. This chapter reserves the complete pool up front and reads cached rows in logical token order.

A token's index in the sequence being processed. It determines the token's rotary position and its place in the attention context; moving its cached row to another physical page does not change that index.

The mapping from a logical cache page to its physical page. Here it is an immutable permutation of the reserved pages, so distinct logical pages cannot overwrite one another. A token keeps its offset within the selected page.

A reserved storage region for a fixed number of token positions across the cache's batch lanes, shared K/V heads and features. Its index locates data in the key and value arrays; it does not specify logical token order.
Allocated slots after the live prefix within its last active KV page. They hold no live rows yet. This portion is zero for an empty prefix or a prefix ending exactly at a page boundary.
A reserved cache page containing no live token rows. In this chapter's eager pool it remains allocated, and its K/V slots count as unused payload.
The scalar slots in the key and value buffers being counted, or their numerical bytes. Counts combine both arrays using shared K/V heads; they exclude metadata, other allocations and process RAM.

Allocate every cache page when creating the cache, before the sequence fills it. Unused pages remain allocated, and rounding a logical capacity up to complete pages can reserve more payload than a contiguous cache.
